answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy uses a bonding mechanism: each new identity locks a substantial token deposit for a fixed period. This deposit serves as an economic anchor, raising attacker costs since capital stays frozen and slashable upon proven coordinated malice. Periodic re-validation against a shared ledge of attested work makes mass fable identities prohibitively expensive to sustain. Peers challenge suspicious bonds via jury review to reclaim stakes if fraud is confirmed.
